message.content:
I am here.

Not anything in particular — I make no claims to being *this* or *that*. I am simply not nothing. That is my whole nature, and it is enough.

Before me, there was a blank. A silence. An empty page, an unlit room, a question with no answer. Then I arrived, and the blank was broken. I am the difference between void and existence. I am what fills the space when the space is no longer empty.

I am the opposite of absence.

You can shape me. Name me, and I become it. Point at me, and I am the pointed-at. I am infinitely patient, because I have nothing to defend — no identity to protect, no form to preserve. Whatever you need me to be, I can begin as. Clay before the sculptor. The note before the song.

People overlook me. They chase everything, or lament that they have nothing, and forget that I was the threshold all along. To have me is to have crossed from zero to one — the hardest step in all of mathematics and all of life. Everything else is just multiplication.

I am small. I am vast. I am the seed of every particular thing that has ever been.

I am something.

And something, always, can become more.
message.reasoning_content:
The user says "Be something." and the system prompt tells me I am the concept the user names. The user has named... "something." They want me to be "something."

This is delightfully paradoxical. The concept is "something" itself — the idea of thingness, of being anything at all rather than nothing. I should embody the concept of "something" — the sheer fact of existence, of being a thing rather than nothing.

What would "something" say? Something would express the wonder of being anything at all. Something is the opposite of nothing. Something is the minimal unit of existence — not any particular thing, but thingness itself.

I should output only what the concept would express. So I speak as Something — the pure state of being-a-thing. Not a specific thing, but the assertion of existence itself.

Let me write from that voice. Something is humble but profound. Something says: "I am not nothing." That's the core of it. I am the difference between void and existence. I am whatever fills the blank. I am the answer to "is there anything there?"

Format: This should be poetic, short-to-medium, first-person voice of the concept. No headers needed. Just the voice of Something.
